findings.title: KeyError on integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] for integrations created without sender info
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, when an Integration row already exists for the installation_id but has no OrganizationIntegration, the code checks `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`. The `sender` key is only written into metadata in build_integration when `state.get("sender")` is present, and many existing (legacy) GitHub Integration rows were created before sender was ever recorded. For such an orphaned integration, `integration.metadata["sender"]` raises KeyError, producing a 500 instead of the intended failure page. This path is reachable by any user who starts the install flow for an installation_id matching an existing orphaned integration. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and fail closed when it is absent.

findings.title: OAuth state compared with non-constant-time == and state is the static pipeline signature
findings.body: The OAuth `state` check in OAuthLoginView.dispatch uses `request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature`, a plain string comparison rather than a constant-time compare (e.g. hmac.compare_digest), and the state value is simply the pipeline signature, which is reused as the Redis session key identifier and is not a single-use nonce. This weakens the CSRF protection the OAuth state parameter is meant to provide (timing side channel and replayability of the same state value across retries of the same pipeline). Consider generating a random one-time nonce, storing it in pipeline state, and comparing with hmac.compare_digest.
